title: How to combine load/discharge itinerary lines of multiple cargoes into a single port record?
text: You may notice that a voyage with multiple cargoes loading (or discharging) at the same port will result in multiple Load/Discharge ports in the voyage itinerary. [image] You can combine, and delete the duplicate itinerary lines using the below steps: In the Cargo tab of the itinerary, right-click on the first cargo handling line of the relevant port, and select Split Cargo Handling Line : [image] Copy the information of the second cargo to the new cargo handling line: [image] Back to the Port/Date tab of the itinerary, select Delete Port : [image] You will now have only one itinerary line that has the information of both cargoes: [image]

title: How to Default the Laycan To Field to 2359 for New Cargoes
text: By default, IMOS sets the Laycan To date field with a time of 00:00. Many operators prefer to default this to 23:59, as laycans are conventionally understood to expire at the end of the stated date. Requiring traders to manually enter 23:59 every time they create a cargo is tedious and prone to error. This behaviour can be changed globally through a single configuration flag. The configuration flag (CFGLaycanDurationInclusive) needs to be disabled, i.e. turn its status to N. Once this is done, then the "Laycan to" field will default to 23:59 for new cargoes. [image] Steps: Navigate to Module Center > Configuration Flags. Search for the flag: CFGLaycanDurationInclusive. Change the flag's status to N (disabled). Save the change. Create a new cargo to verify that the Laycan To field now defaults to 23:59. Note: This change applies to new cargoes only. Existing cargo records are not retroactively updated.

title: How to include Financial Attachments in Voyages
text: For attachments that are specific to individual invoices, they can be added within individual financial invoices. If you would like to add more general attachments that do not apply to any invoice specifically, you can do so under Voyage Attachments. [image] If you would like to segregate finance-related attachments from the rest, you can consider using Voyage Notes in the Voyage Manager with the category "Finance" (which needs to be created in the Data Center > Note Categories). You can then add the relevant attachments to the voyage note itself. [image][image]

title: How to invoice an external charterer for whole or parts of freight using Spot Out?
text: When performing a SPOT voyage, you may need to invoice an external charterer for the whole or parts of the total freight. You can do this using the Create Spot Out functionality to include a linked Cargo contract to your VC In. When you right-click on the VC In in the Cargoes grid of a SPOT voyage, you will see a Create Spot Out option. Clicking Create Spot Out will create a new cargo and automatically add it to the voyage; this newly created cargo will also be automatically linked to the original VC In as a relet. Once the necessary details are filled out in the linked Cargo contract, you will be able to create a freight invoice for the counterparty. [image]

title: How to search Port Expenses excluding rebills
text: It is possible to search port expenses and exclude options listed within the Port Expense search screen. Right click the port in question and then select the option Port Expense Search. [image] On the Port Expense Search screen, chose the drop down menu Expense Type. Here you can choose the type of expenses to include and exclude. [image]

title: How to select the correct freight when there are multiple freight rate options in Cargo/COA.
text: There are occasions where in Cargo/CP/COA, there are multiple freight rates, but only one is the most suitable for a specific voyage. On the CP details on the "Itin. Options" all the possible loading and discharging ports must be defined. [image] Then, on the "Pricing" tab all the possible combinations of loading and discharging option must be defined. [image] In the end, the system will automatically reflect the rate that matches the combination of what exists in the voyage's itinerary and what has been defined in the CP details

title: How to set up Port Activities ROBs to drive the Carbon Calculator (MRV/Berth-to-Berth)
text: IMOS, by default, calculates and captures consumption figures as Port to Port. With regulations that leverage MRV, such as FuelEU and EU ETS, Berth-to-Berth logic is required. To capture this information accurately, IMOS references PS, AF, LL, and PE Action Types and the ROBs to calculate Berth Consumption. The overall structure of the Port Activities should be structured as follows: PS to AF (Sea), AF to LL (Port), and LL to PE (Sea) [image] If this structure is not met, the carbon calculator will not be based on Berth-to-Berth logic required by the EU regulations. Setup: The required Activity Types (PS, AF, LL, PE) and capturing corresponding ROBs can be defined under Data Center > Port Activities via the Act Type and ROBs columns. [image]

title: IMOS - Configurations to be updated at the start of a new calendar year
text: At the start of each new calendar year, you may need to check and update the following configurations: Account Periods - create a new record in the Account Periods for the new year. Invoice Number - Go to Financials > Document Numbers and verify that the Reference Year is up-to-date. Voyage Number - If your system has both CFGVoyageNoFormat and CFGUseGlobalVoyageNumbering enabled at the same time, you may notice that the voyage number for voyages created in the new calendar year is not updated. To reference the new year: Disable CFGUseGlobalVoyageNumbering, create a new voyage, then re-enable CFGUseGlobalVoyageNumbering.

title: IMOS - Why does my freight invoice reflect CP Qty although CP terms say Bill By: BL Qty?
text: In the event where the BL Qty or Invoice Qty is higher than the CP Qty, it is important to set up the overage term in the CP Terms Details to ensure proper freight calculation. If the overage term is not set up, the freight for the excess loaded cargo will not be calculated. If the BL Qty or Invoice Qty is within the CP Qty amount and no overage should be charged, then you will need to check your Cargo Tolerance Options Type set under the CP Terms Details. Another reason is that we default the BL Qty used in the calculation to the CP Qty when there are ANY loading activities at that port that have not been lifted.

title: Unable to complete a voyage due to an error message "Activity reports have been entered after port departure at the last port"
text: [image] When a voyage is scheduled to be marked as "Completed," it is crucial that the final activity report is either a "T" (Terminating) or a "D" (Departure) type form. If the final activity report does not fall into either of these categories, an error message will be displayed. To resolve this issue, the user should navigate to the last departure port and delete any activity report that is not of type "T" or "D."

title: What does "Failed to include cargo info in fixture notification XML" mean when trying to save a voyage?
text: There are two potential causes: The counterparty specified on the cargo contract does not match up with an address book entry. The cargo type specified on the cargo contract does not match up with a "Cargo" in the data center. [image] If you run into this message, double check the Counterparty and the Cargo to ensure that they still exist and are valid entries.

title: What does Failed to synchronize cargo data mean?
text: Failed to synchronize cargo data. Cannot synchronize cargo itinerary. Non-commercial data for port, cannot be changed. Unable to update CP terms for trade unit. [image] The error means the itinerary row is locked for a specified port. This can be due to the vessel sailed from the port or you have port or bunker expenses linked to it.

title: What does it mean when a transit port (port function P or I) is light blue in the itinerary?
text: If a transit port in an itinerary is light blue, it means that the port function (P or I) has been manually entered for this port (as opposed to being automatically populated by IMOS). It also means that the transit port is locked. [image]

title: What is the source of the Company column data in the Claims List?
text: For claims linked to standard Voyages: If the claim is a Laytime Claim, then the value from the Voyage Manager > Properties > Company field will be used. If the claim is a "normal" Claim, then the value from the Claim > Claim tab > Company field will be used.

title: Why am I not able to change the voyage status from "Completed" to "Commenced"?
text: There may be an instance whereby you are trying to change a voyage status from Completed to Commenced and notice that the status keeps changing automatically. This happens when you have CFGAutoCompleteVoyage enabled and have entered the departure Date/Time for the last port of call for the voyage. You can change this behavior by changing the value of the configuration flag to N. [image]

title: Why am I unable to add a commencing port?
text: In the below example, the voyage has already commenced. Given the vessel is currently at the loading port it is not possible to add another port before this. [image] In order to add another port before the loading port, any Port Activities and Activity Reports need to be deleted or the voyage status needs to be changed to "Scheduled".

title: Why am I unable to save a voyage after correcting errors and warnings?
text: When utilizing the Voyage Manager tool, if a user creates a voyage with missing data or unpopulated fields and a red or yellow icon appears, this represents an Error or Warning. If the user makes corrections and attempts to save but gets stuck, they must: refresh the page, copy the Estimate from which the Voyage is based, delete the current Voyage, and then schedule a new Voyage from the newly created Estimate.

title: Why am I unable to update the "Chtr Specialist" field?
text: The Chtr Specialist field in the Voyage Manager is driven by the Voyage Fixture in the Chartering Module. [image] To modify the Chrtr Specialist field, the Voyage Fixture object rights needs to be given to the user. Having full object rights to the Voyage Manager will not enable a user to update this field since its permission is tied to the Voyage Fixture. [image][image]

title: Why are my Emission Expenses missing from Voyage P&L when "Include in PnL" checkbox is selected?
text: When the Include in PnL checkbox is selected, but there is no value within the Voyage P&L, please check the TC emissions tab. [image] The Value here in Settlement Type should be anything EXCEPT N/A. If this value is N/A, Emissions are always excluded from the Voyage P&L. [image]

title: Why are the Voyage P&L (Act) and Voyage P&L (Est) columns blank in the Voyages list?
text: These columns will not populate until the following criteria are met: CFGCacheVoyPnl is enabled. A "current" snapshot exists for the voyage. This can be done manually by clicking the "Snapshot" button in the Voyage P&L. Once the above has been set up, be sure to save the voyage as this will update several reporting outlets in the database with the accurate figures.

title: Why can't I access Demurrage Root Cause Analysis?
text: The Access Rights Demurrage: Demurrage Activity and Demurrage: Root Cause Analysis must both be configured to in order to have access to the Demurrage Root Cause Analysis workspace. Having access to only Demurrage Root Cause Analysis is not enough.
